C45233.observed: What was checked: what the window for splitting a quantity across bins actually offers. What happened: it is headed "Bin Locations", names the part it is for, and lays out one row per bin under three headings - BIN NAME, QUANTITY IN STOCK and AMOUNT. The row shows the bin's name, a "Default" badge marking it as the default bin, how many are in stock, and a box to type how many to take from it. Underneath it states plainly what will happen - "Allocated 2 — the row quantity will be set to 2" - and it offers three actions: "Auto", "Cancel" and "Apply".
C45233.not_observed: What "Auto" does when it has somewhere to redistribute to - filling the default bin first and then the largest - could not be seen: every stocked part on this branch is held in a single bin, so there is nothing to spread across.

C45234.observed: What was checked: whether pressing Apply actually carries the allocation back to the row, and what it does to the quantity. What happened: with 2 allocated in the Bin Locations window, Apply closed it and the row came back showing the bin chip and a quantity of 2 - the total of what was allocated. The window says so before you press it, too: "Allocated 2 — the row quantity will be set to 2". So the quantity always agrees with the bins it is being taken from.
